1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Exam Technique and Final Review, the last module of the course. There is no new task statement here. You know the content; this module is about turning what you know into points: how to pace, read, eliminate and answer, and how to use your last week.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Pace the sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes with checkpoints. Use a four-step method: read, predict, eliminate, confirm. Handle multiple-response questions, qualifier words and look-alike traps. And plan your final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom's Mock Exam
1.text: A teammate at Lantern and Loom sat a practice exam and finished just under the pass mark. The review showed lost points, not lost knowledge: misread questions, look-alike services and blank answers. The course content is covered; now technique has to match it. Your job is to turn what you know into points.

1.title: The Exam Clock
1.text: Start with the clock. Sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes is about two minutes each. Aim for about one hundred seconds on a first pass; the spare time is for long scenarios and review. The figure shows three checkpoints, as the latest you should reach: question twenty by minute forty, question forty by minute eighty, and question sixty-five by minute one hundred twenty, which leaves time to review. Fifteen questions are unscored, and you cannot tell which, so treat every one as real. Exam tip: if you are behind at a checkpoint, answer quickly and move on; a blank always scores zero.

1.title: Read for the Requirement
1.text: Read the last line first, because it holds what is being asked; this is a tip from A W S's own certification blog. Then read the scenario and underline the requirement words: most cost-effective, least operational overhead, highest availability, most secure. Note the verb, such as encrypt, decouple, cache, fail over, migrate or restrict. Note the constraint: Region, downtime allowed, budget or existing skills. Then predict the answer before you look at the options. Exam tip: the scenario is the story; the last line is the test.

1.title: A Four-Step Answer Method
1.text: Use the same four steps for every question. The figure shows them as four chevrons. Read: the last line first, then the scenario. Predict: name the service or pattern before you see the options. Eliminate: remove the options that are clearly wrong. Confirm: match the requirement word and the verb to what is left. Exam tip: a prediction stops a plausible distractor from pulling you off course.

1.title: Eliminating Distractors
1.text: Distractors are real services that sound plausible, so ask why each one fails. Wrong job: it does something else, such as S Q S buffering while S N S fans out. Wrong scope: a Multi-A Z fix for a Region failure, or the reverse. Over-engineered: Multi-Region active-active when a backup meets the goal. Self-managed: E C two with custom code when a managed service fits. Half true: one clause fits and another does not. Words such as always and never deserve a second look. Exam tip: remove two of four options and a guess is right half the time.

1.title: Multiple-Response Questions
1.text: The exam has two question types. Multiple choice has one correct answer and three distractors. Multiple response has two or more correct answers among five or more options. The question tells you how many to choose, such as Select two. Judge each option on its own, true or false against the question, then count. Choose exactly the number asked. If three options fit, reread the question for the qualifier that rules one out. Exam tip: two correct answers are often one for each part of the requirement.

1.title: Qualifier Words Steer the Answer
1.text: Qualifier words pick one correct answer from several that work. Most cost-effective points to Spot, Savings Plans, lifecycle rules, serverless, right-sizing and gateway endpoints. Least operational overhead points to managed and serverless services: Lambda, Fargate, Aurora and S Q S. Highest availability points to Multi-A Z and Auto Scaling, with Multi-Region only if the Region must survive. Most secure and least privilege point to I A M roles, K M S, private subnets and narrow policies. Lowest latency points to CloudFront, Global Accelerator, caches and a closer Region. Decouple points to S Q S, S N S and Event Bridge. And minimal downtime points to blue green deployment, replication and Multi-A Z failover. Exam tip: underline the qualifier.

1.title: Architecture Question Shortcuts
1.text: Most questions are pattern matching, so name the symptom first, then the fix. Spiky load and dropped requests: queue it and use Auto Scaling. Slow worldwide users: CloudFront or Global Accelerator. A read-heavy database: read replicas and caching. Data in S three that must be locked down: a bucket policy, Block Public Access, K M S and a V P C endpoint. A single zone failure that takes the app down: Multi-A Z and Auto Scaling. Who did it, and what changed: CloudTrail and Config. And a bill that is too high: right-size, Savings Plans, lifecycle rules and endpoints. Exam tip: name the symptom first, then the fix.

1.title: Choosing Between Two Valid Answers
1.text: When two answers both work, ask which one is simpler, managed and cheaper. Prefer serverless and managed services over E C two you operate. Prefer I A M roles over access keys, and least privilege over broad access. Prefer the design that meets the stated goal and no more, because extra Regions and tiers cost money. Check the scope: account, Region, Availability Zone or instance. And make sure nothing in the option breaks a stated constraint. Exam tip: the best answer meets every stated requirement with the least effort and cost.

1.title: When You Are Unsure
1.text: Never leave a question blank. The exam guide says an unanswered question counts as incorrect, and a guess has no penalty. Eliminate first, then choose between what is left. When two answers fit, prefer the one that is managed, least privilege and simplest. Change an answer only when you find a specific reason. And if the screen lets you mark a question to revisit, use it for hard ones, and check the exam tutorial. Exam tip: a blank always scores zero; a guess might not.

2.title: Your Final Week
2.text: Plan your last week. Seven days out, read the current exam guide again and check for changes. Six to four days out, redo the questions for your two weakest domains and write your own look-alike notes. Three days out, take a timed run of about sixty-five questions in one hundred thirty minutes; A W S offers practice question sets. Two days out, read Module fifteen once, then say the lists aloud. The day before, do a light review, get a good night's sleep and sort out your exam-day logistics. Exam tip: practice under the clock, because pace is a skill that improves with repetition.

2.title: Exam Day and Afterwards
2.text: On exam day, you take the exam at a Pearson Vue test center, or online with a proctor; read the provider's rules. The fee is one hundred fifty U S dollars, and a pass is valid for three years. Results are posted to your A W S Certification Account within five business days after the exam, unless held for review. If you do not pass, wait fourteen calendar days; there is no limit on attempts, and each one needs the full fee. If you pass, you cannot retake the same exam for two years. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, A W S may change fees and policies, so read its pages before you book. Exam tip: policies and fees change, so check before you book.

2.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom's Mock Exam
2.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Ran short of time in the last ten questions: use checkpoints, question twenty by minute forty, and forty by minute eighty. Chose Multi-Region for highest availability in one Region: read the scope, because Multi-A Z meets a zone failure. Picked one answer in a Select two question: judge each option and choose exactly two. Built a custom queue on E C two: read the qualifier, because least overhead means managed. Left three questions blank: answer every one, since there is no penalty. And chose S N S to buffer a spike: read the verb, because buffering is S Q S.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Pace: sixty-five questions, one hundred thirty minutes, about two minutes each, with checkpoints. Method: read the last line, predict, eliminate, confirm. Types: multiple choice and multiple response. Traps: look-alike services, qualifier words, wrong scope and over-engineering. When unsure: never leave a blank, since there is no penalty for guessing. And plan a final week, exam day and, if needed, a retake after fourteen days.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Lantern and Loom's order intake drops requests during sales. The team wants to absorb the spikes with the least operational overhead. Which solution fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: an Amazon S Q S queue ahead of Lambda consumers. The requirement words are absorb spikes and least operational overhead. S Q S buffers the orders, and Lambda scales its consumers with no servers.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Select two. Lantern and Loom's web tier is one E C two instance, and its database is a single-A Z R D S instance. The goal is to survive the loss of one Availability Zone with the least change. Which two actions help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and B. Turn on Multi-A Z for the database, and run the web tier in an Auto Scaling group across two zones behind a load balancer. A larger instance, a same-zone replica and longer retention do not survive a zone loss.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A Lambda function must read objects from one S three bucket and nothing else. Which approach follows the exam's least-privilege preference? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: attach a role that allows read access to only that bucket. It gives temporary credentials and the narrowest permission. Embedded keys, administrator access and a public bucket all break least privilege.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. With six minutes left, a candidate has four questions unanswered and is unsure of each. Based on the exam guide's scoring rules, what should they do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: answer all four. The exam guide says unanswered questions are scored as incorrect and there is no penalty for guessing. A guess can only help; a blank always scores zero.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Select two. Which two statements about S A A scoring are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are C and E. The exam includes fifty scored and fifteen unscored questions that are not identified, and unanswered questions count as incorrect. Guessing has no penalty, scoring is compensatory across domains, and the minimum passing score is seven hundred twenty.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: C. Question two: A and B. Question three: D. Question four: B. Question five: C and E. That completes the course. Review Module fifteen, practice under the clock, answer every question, and good luck on exam day.
